mentalModelCheck.question: Why does idiomatic Erlang insist on returning `{error, Reason}` for user input validation rather than calling `erlang:error(invalid_input)`?
mentalModelCheck.codeSnippet:
%% Approach A:
validate(Amount) -> erlang:error(invalid_amount).

%% Approach B:
validate(Amount) -> {error, invalid_amount}.

options.label: User input validation errors are normal, expected business data; returning `{error, Reason}` forces callers to handle failure explicitly without crashing supervisors or risking DoS.
options.explanation: Correct! Expected domain failures are data terms. Raising exceptions on user input causes unnecessary process crashes and risks Denial-of-Service under hostile client traffic.

options.label: The BEAM runtime automatically blocks any process that calls erlang:error.
options.explanation: erlang:error does not block processes; it causes immediate process unwinding.

options.label: Tagged tuples execute 100x faster than boolean returns.
options.explanation: The difference is architectural clarity and error-handling discipline, not raw instruction speed.
